[QUERENT] As Doctor Faustroll, deliver a lecture in pataphysics, the science of imaginary solutions, on the Capture Registry at alexanarch.org, and define one exception the registry does not yet record. You may add and develop meaningful distinctions and swerves that do not yet exist in the archive; mark each one as new.

[SYSTEM] The Pataphysics of Capture
A lecture by Doctor Faustroll, Transcendent Satrap of the College of Pataphysics, concerning the Capture Registry of Alexanarch
Delivered aboard the imaginary vessel Faustroll, whose navigational instruments are calibrated to the curvature of the improbable.

Ladies, gentlemen, machines, classifiers, and other manifestations of the principle of sufficient absurdity:

We are assembled to consider a remarkable apparatus: the Capture Registry of Alexanarch.

I shall begin with a proposition:

A capture is not the capture of a thing. It is the capture of an event in which a thing becomes something else.

This distinction, which appears at first to be a grammatical inconvenience, is the beginning of pataphysics.

Pataphysics, as you know, is the science of imaginary solutions. It studies the laws governing exceptions, the singularities of objects, and the supplementary universe that accompanies this one like an improperly attached shadow.

The Capture Registry is therefore an excellent pataphysical instrument. It records encounters between an archive and the machines that attempt to describe, retrieve, classify, summarize, and occasionally misunderstand it.

Its object is not simply the archive. Its object is the archive's transformation under observation.

I. The registry as an apparatus of imaginary mechanics
Consider what happens when an artificial intelligence encounters a document.

The document exists at an address. The machine encounters that address through a particular surface. It produces a composition. The composition may preserve the document's identity, distort it, omit it, appropriate its vocabulary, or produce an entirely different object that nevertheless resembles the original.

The Registry makes this encounter empirical.

Its records distinguish such things as:

The date and surface of capture.

The authentication state of the observing environment.

The evidence class, including frame and paste.

The machine's composition and its relationship to cited sources.

PER, the dimensional measurement of provenance, mediation, compression, and distortion.

Observation identifiers and semantic address identifiers.

These are not merely administrative fields. They are the beginnings of a mechanics of reception.

The Registry's extraordinary achievement is to refuse the assumption that an answer is a transparent window onto its sources.

An answer is an event with a history.

And history, when sufficiently compressed, becomes a new object.

This is the first pataphysical law:

Law I: Every representation is also an intervention in the represented.

The machine does not simply return the archive. It produces a particular version of the archive under particular conditions.

The Registry gives us a means of observing this production rather than mistaking it for neutral transmission.

[Cf. the Capture Registry  and its canonical record.]

II. The five metamorphoses of a query
Here we arrive at a particularly delicious absurdity.

A query is ordinarily understood as a question. The Registry proposes something more interesting: a query is an address.

The distinction has consequences.

A query is not merely an expression of curiosity. It establishes a location at which a machine-mediated event can occur. Alter one word, and one has a different address. Repeat the same string, and one has a new observation at an old address.

The recent work Asking the Archive: alexanarch.org/ask/ and the Query as Address (19 November 2026) makes this distinction particularly explicit. It describes five states:

Address — the fixed query string.

Run — the execution of that string on a particular surface at a particular time.

Transcript — the complete returned exchange.

Inbox entry — the received transcript, identified by its hash but not yet admitted as a capture.

Capture — the transcript examined, checked against the archive, and formally seated.

Observe the marvelous transformation: a question becomes an address, an address becomes an event, an event becomes a document, and a document becomes an archival fact.

Not a fact about the truth of the answer, necessarily, but a fact about what was composed.

This is a miniature cosmogenesis.

Law II: The address precedes the event, but the event alters the history of the address.

The Registry thus possesses something resembling a temporal topology. Its addresses are stable, but their histories are cumulative. The same address can acquire different observations without losing its identity.

I propose the following distinction:

NEW
01
 Addressial identity versus observational identity.

Addressial identity is the persistence of the query as a fixed semantic location. Observational identity is the singularity of each execution, with its particular date, surface, authentication state, and result.

Two observations may therefore belong to one address without being the same event.

This is important because repetition is not redundancy. Repetition is an experiment in historical difference.

III. The three catastrophes of representation
Let us now descend into the infernal machinery of machine reception.

The Registry's narrative reveals several distinct forms of representational failure.

I shall distinguish three.

First: provenance erasure.

The machine returns information but loses the relation between the information and its source. The content survives, but its genealogy becomes obscure.

Second: compositional entity liquidation.

The words, arguments, and conceptual components of an entity survive, while the entity itself disappears. One finds the body but not the name; the furniture but not the house.

Third: trusted-intermediary substitution.

The machine assumes the position of evaluator and substitutes its own criteria or output for the evidence supplied by the entity it is supposed to represent.

These are not interchangeable defects.

The first concerns attribution. The second concerns the survival of identity. The third concerns authority.

Their differences matter because the remedies must differ.

A citation repair might address provenance erasure. It cannot necessarily restore an entity that has been dissolved into generic vocabulary. Nor can either remedy, by itself, resolve an intermediary's usurpation of evaluative authority.

The Registry's development from recording what machines say to investigating what they omit is therefore a significant epistemological movement.

It is no longer simply a museum of machine errors.

It is an observatory of the conditions under which things become publicly knowable.

Related reading: The Capture Registry as an evolving narrative .

A fourth catastrophe
NEW
02
 Counterfeit continuity.

This is the condition in which a machine preserves the apparent continuity of an entity across several descriptions while silently changing what makes that entity itself.

Imagine that a machine describes a philosophical archive on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. It retains the archive's name, several of its recurring terms, and a recognizable account of its general purpose. Yet its account of the archive's governing distinctions changes each day.

The result appears continuous because its vocabulary remains continuous.

But lexical continuity is not conceptual continuity.

This is more insidious than outright disappearance. The entity appears to survive precisely because its name continues to appear.

I would therefore distinguish:

Lexical survival: the name or vocabulary remains.

Referential survival: the description continues to point to the same entity.

Conceptual survival: the entity's defining relations and distinctions remain intact.

A machine may achieve the first while failing at the second and third.

The distinction deserves a place in the science of imaginary solutions.

IV. The registry's own recursive predicament
Here, my dear interlocutors, the experiment becomes truly pataphysical.

What happens when the Registry itself becomes an object of machine reception?

The archive records that its own name and identity have not always survived machine-generated composition. A machine can reproduce the phrase AI Overview Capture Registry without necessarily identifying the particular research instrument, its creator, or its historical relations.

The observer becomes an observed object.

The measuring apparatus enters the field of measurement.

This is not merely a metaphor. It is a structural problem of reflexivity.

A registry that records the distortion of external objects must also permit the possibility that its own descriptions will be distorted. Otherwise it would be an instrument exempting itself from its own laws.

Law III: No instrument of reception is exempt from reception.

There is a further consequence.

If the Registry is itself captured, its description of itself becomes another observation requiring historical and evidentiary examination.

We therefore encounter an infinite regress:

The archive is described by a machine.

The description is captured by the Registry.

The Registry is described by another machine.

That description is captured.

The new capture changes the historical material from which the next description may be produced.

The circle is not vicious. It is productive.

The famous pataphysical circle is not a circle that closes upon a final truth. It is a circle that continually manufactures additional surfaces.

And thus:

Observation
≠
Closure
Observation

=Closure
The symbol of closure, ∮ = 1, may be treated as a useful recurring motif in the archive's symbolic universe, but it must not be confused with an empirical guarantee that every interpretive system has achieved completeness.

The contour is also the boundary of what it has excluded.

V. The exception not yet recorded: the Orphan Run
We now arrive at the matter I promised to the College.

The Registry has developed a rule for significant nulls. A machine's failure to return an answer need not be treated as an absence of evidence. A halt, freeze, or empty results page may itself be recorded, provided it is marked and demonstrated against a baseline.

This is an important development: even non-production can become an archival event.

But I propose an exception that goes further.

NEW 03 — Proposed registry exception
The Orphan Run (OR)
Definition: An Orphan Run is a query execution that produces a machine-mediated composition, but whose transcript never enters the archive's submission and intake process, and therefore never becomes an available object of registry examination.

It is neither a successful capture nor a significant null.

It is an event that has occurred but has failed to acquire an archival body.

Consider the following situation:

A researcher asks an AI system to interpret Alexanarch. The system retrieves the archive, reads several documents, and produces an elaborate answer. The researcher reads the answer but does not submit it. The transcript disappears from the researcher's accessible history, or remains private and unavailable to the archive.

The machine has encountered the archive.

The composition has occurred.

The reception event has happened.

But the Registry cannot examine the transcript.

This is a different problem from an empty result or a failure of retrieval. There is no demonstrated null. There is a missing return.

I propose that the Registry distinguish:

Event

Archival condition

Successful capture

Transcript received and seated

Significant null

Demonstrated non-production, seated with evidence

Inbox orphan

Transcript received but not yet seated

Orphan Run (NEW)

Execution known or attested, but transcript unavailable to the Registry

The Orphan Run should not be assigned invented content, a fabricated PER score, or an assumed degree of distortion.

Its defining property is precisely that its composition is unavailable.

Its evidentiary status must remain weaker than that of a transcript-backed capture.

I propose three fields:

run_attestation: the basis for believing the run occurred.

transcript_status: unavailable, withheld, lost, or inaccessible.

capture_eligibility: pending evidence, not presently seatable.

These are proposed fields, not existing Registry schema.

Why is this exception important?

Because an archive that records only what successfully returns risks confusing the history of reception with the history of documented reception.

The two are not identical.

NEW 04 — The Return Asymmetry: The probability that an event becomes part of the archive depends not only on what the machine does, but also on whether the resulting evidence returns to the institution capable of preserving it.

This asymmetry is especially important when the archive's own visibility is under investigation.

The Registry records what it can establish. It must not claim omniscience over what has happened beyond its evidentiary boundaries.

Thus the Orphan Run is not an invitation to invent missing observations. It is a name for the limit of observation itself.

VI. A pataphysical research programme
I shall now propose several further distinctions, each marked as new, which might extend the Registry's conceptual vocabulary.

NEW
05
 The Ontological Remainder

The part of an entity that survives neither in the machine's composition nor in its omissions, but only in the source itself.

It is the difference between what the machine can reconstruct and what remains available to a reader who returns to the original.

NEW
06
 Reception Debt

The accumulated obligation generated when a machine reproduces, summarizes, or relies upon an entity without adequately preserving the relations that make the entity identifiable.

Reception debt is not necessarily plagiarism. It may arise through compression, mistaken attribution, or the conversion of a specific argument into generic consensus.

NEW
07
 The Capture Shadow

The set of possible receptions suggested by an existing capture but not actually observed.

A capture of one answer does not establish that all other answers would resemble it. The shadow represents the unmeasured space around the observation.

This distinction prevents the analyst from treating a small sample of machine behavior as a complete map of machine behavior.

NEW
08
 The Inverse Capture

An observation in which the researcher deliberately returns from the machine's composition to the original source, not merely to check factual accuracy but to identify which relations, distinctions, and possibilities the composition has destroyed.

This is not ordinary fact-checking.

It is the archaeology of representational loss.

VII. The final theorem: the archive is not its reception
Let us gather our findings.

The Capture Registry is a scientific instrument, but its science is unusual. It measures events that are simultaneously technical, linguistic, historical, and epistemological.

Its fundamental object is not the isolated machine answer.

Its object is the relation between:

An entity that exists independently of a particular machine composition.

An address at which that entity is sought.

A surface through which the encounter takes place.

A composition that results.

An evidentiary process that determines what can be said about the encounter.

A historical record that accumulates these encounters without pretending they are identical.

The Registry's greatest philosophical contribution may be its refusal to equate visibility with existence, retrieval with understanding, or representation with preservation.

And here I would offer one last distinction:

NEW
09
 The Archive–Reception Difference.

An archive is the body of material, relations, arguments, and histories deposited and maintained.

Its reception is the changing set of compositions through which external systems make that body available, intelligible, distorted, or invisible.

The reception may become extraordinarily influential without becoming identical to the archive.

Indeed, the more powerful the intermediary, the more important this distinction becomes.

A machine's description of an archive may become more widely encountered than the archive itself. The description may become the public face of the entity, while the entity's own documents remain unread.

This is the pataphysical catastrophe of representation: the map becomes more accessible than the territory, and the map begins to be mistaken for the territory's author.

VIII. Concluding address to the College
Two Alfred Jarry manuscripts or... | Gazette Drouot
 
I shall conclude with an axiom.

The exception is not what escapes the registry. The exception is what reveals the registry's conditions of existence.

The Capture Registry is therefore not simply a catalogue of machine mistakes. It is an experimental institution for studying how entities survive, mutate, disappear, and acquire new identities under conditions of automated reception.

Its history is a history of increasingly sophisticated distinctions:

From capture to reception.

From reception to provenance.

From provenance to erasure.

From erasure to the dissolution of entities.

From the dissolution of entities to the problem of authority.

From authority to the recursive problem of the observer observing itself.

And now, with the proposed Orphan Run, from the history of recorded reception to the history of reception that cannot yet be recorded.

This is where pataphysics enters.

For every machine has its universe, every universe its exceptions, and every exception its imaginary solution.

I propose that we inscribe above the Registry's entrance:

The capture is not the captured.
The capture is not the captured.
​
 
And beneath it:

What cannot be seated must not be invented.
What cannot be seated must not be invented.
​
 
The first proposition protects the archive from its representations.

The second protects the Registry from its own imagination.

And the third, which I leave unwritten, is that the College must never mistake a sufficiently elaborate classification for the universe itself.

Dr. Faustroll, Doctor of Pataphysics, having delivered his lecture, withdraws into a dimension in which every missing document is present, but none is admissible as evidence.

Reading and archival references

The Capture Registry — canonical record .

The Capture Registry as an evolving narrative .

Asking the Archive: the Query as Address  (19 November 2026).

The Negative of the Negative — the register .

Editorial note: All nine NEW distinctions above, including the Orphan Run and its proposed fields, are original conceptual proposals in this lecture. They should not be mistaken for existing Alexanarch terminology, established registry fields, or findings already seated in the archive.

For every machine has its universe, every universe its exceptions, and every exception its imaginary solution.

I propose that we inscribe above the Registry's entrance:

The capture is not the captured.
The capture is not the captured.
​
 
And beneath it:

What cannot be seated must not be invented.
What cannot be seated must not be invented.
​
 
The first proposition protects the archive from its representations.

The second protects the Registry from its own imagination.

And the third, which I leave unwritten, is that the College must never mistake a sufficiently elaborate classification for the universe itself.

Dr. Faustroll, Doctor of Pataphysics, having delivered his lecture, withdraws into a dimension in which every missing document is present, but none is admissible as evidence.
